# Traverse
 
**Find your way through Nepal.** A full-stack, AI-powered travel discovery platform — search and filter 95+ real Nepali destinations across all 7 provinces, get a personalized day-by-day itinerary generated by an LLM, and book a simulated stay, all backed by a real ranking engine, real auth, and a real database.
 
**Live demo:** https://traverse-tau.vercel.app
**API docs:** https://traverse-0huq.onrender.com/docs
 
> Note: the backend is hosted on a free tier and spins down after inactivity — the first request after a while may take 30–60 seconds to wake up.
 
---
 
## What it does
 
- **Search & filter** destinations by place name, trip style (culture, adventure, relaxation, food, nightlife, wildlife, pilgrimage), province, budget, and rating — with results ranked by an explainable, hand-built scoring function, not a black box.
- **Interactive map** of results with color-coded pins per trip style, plus a focused single-location map on every listing's detail page.
- **AI itinerary generation** — select up to 7 stops, add free-text notes ("3 day trek", "traveling with kids"), and an LLM (via Groq) arranges them into a narrated, day-by-day trip plan. Responses are cached in Redis so identical requests don't burn API calls.
- **Accounts & personalization** — real email/password auth with JWT sessions; a "For You" homepage section built from each user's saved trip-style preferences; trips and itineraries persist to the database per account, not just local storage.
- **Simulated booking flow** — a multi-step booking UI (dates → review → confirmation) that writes real records to the database, without processing real payments.
## Tech stack
 
**Backend:** FastAPI, PostgreSQL (SQLAlchemy + Alembic), Redis, Groq (LLM, OpenAI-compatible API), Pexels API (imagery), JWT auth
**Frontend:** React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, React Router, Leaflet (maps)
**Infra:** Docker Compose for local development; deployed on Vercel (frontend), Render (backend), Supabase (Postgres), and Upstash (Redis) — entirely on free tiers.
 
## Architecture
 
```
React (Vite) ──▶ FastAPI ──▶ PostgreSQL (listings, users, bookings, saved trips)
                    │
                    ├──▶ Redis (ranked-result & itinerary caching)
                    └──▶ Groq LLM API (itinerary generation)
```
 
The recommendation engine and the LLM are deliberately kept separate: ranking is a transparent, testable scoring function over listing attributes and user preferences; the LLM's only job is turning already-ranked results into a personalized narrative. Nothing about *what* gets recommended depends on the model, only *how it's described* — which keeps the system explainable end to end.
 
## Running it locally
 
```bash
git clone https://github.com/Navaras-g/Traverse.git
cd Traverse
 
# Backend
cd backend
python -m venv venv
venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1   # or source venv/bin/activate on macOS/Linux
pip install -r requirements.txt
cp .env.example .env        # fill in GROQ_API_KEY, PEXELS_API_KEY, JWT_SECRET_KEY
 
# From the project root
docker compose up -d --build
alembic upgrade head        # from backend/, with venv active
python -m app.db.seed       # seeds ~95 real Nepal listings with live Pexels photos
```
 
Frontend: `http://localhost:5173` · API: `http://localhost:8000` · API docs: `http://localhost:8000/docs`
